units: <cite ref="Chullin 84a:6">Ḥull. 84ᵃ</cite> <he>מחוסר … וג׳</he> requires the acts of pouring out the blood, scraping off the blood stains &c.
<cite ref="Chullin 93a:6">Ib. 93ᵃ</cite> <he>ריש מעיא … בעי ג׳</he> the top of the small bowels up to a cubit’s length must be scraped (in order to remove the fat).

senses.gloss: dragging, pulling, moving an object without lifting.
units: <cite ref="Shabbat 22a">Sabb. 22ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Pesachim 101a">Pes. 101ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Menachot 41b:8">Men. 41ᵇ</cite> <he>הלכה … בג׳</he> the law decides in favor of … with reference to dragging an object on the Sabbath, v. <cite ref="C01392"><he>גָּרַר</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Kiddushin 1:5:12">Y. Kidd. I, 60ᵈ</cite> top <he>מהו שיקנו בג׳</he> can they be taken possession of by moving without lifting?

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 7:6:2">Y. Pes. VII, 34ᶜ</cite> top <he>מאי נפקא … ג׳</he> what is the difference between them? They differ as to the majority of one tribe carrying with it (determining the legal status of) the whole nation, v. <cite ref="C01392"><he>גָּרַר</he></cite> 3.—

<cite ref="Shabbat 71a:3">Sabb. 71ᵃ</cite> <he>ומי אית ליה … ג׳</he> does R. adopt the opinion that one action can be involved with another so as to be considered one continuous act (e.g. cutting grain and immediately grinding it)? <cite ref="Shabbat 71a:3">Ib.</cite> <he>ג׳ דג׳</he> an application of this principle in the second degree, that the action involved should involve a third action.
